name: How to be a tester — Kenya Student Test Week
playIn: watch.html?app=tester&mode=explain (player v3.1 maps app=tester → kenya/_kickoff.json; voice/tester-explain.m4a)
lines: Karibu, and thank you for joining the Daraja Student Test Week. This short video explains what we are asking you to do, and why it matters.
First, what is Daraja? Daraja means bridge in Swahili. Daraja Studio is a small family business in America. It makes simple apps that open in the browser on your phone. There is nothing to install.
The family gives the profits from the apps to help students in Kenya stay in school. So when you test these apps, you are helping students like you.

Many of the apps were made for American families and churches. Some talk about American things, like taxes or health insurance. That is fine. Each video will explain the American words in a simple way.

Why do we test? Because the people who build an app cannot see its problems. They know where every button is. You do not. You are seeing it for the first time, and that is exactly what makes your eyes so valuable.
Each test has four parts, and they always come in the same order.
Part one: a short video, like this one. It explains what the app is for, who uses it, and the main screens. Watch it once, with the sound on.

Part two: the test script. It tells you exactly what to do, one step at a time, and what you should see. After each step, tap It worked, It didn't, or Not sure. If something did not work, say what happened in your own words.

Part three: the final challenge. The app starts empty. You get a few jobs to do, but nobody tells you which buttons to press. You use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work. The checker looks at what the app really saved, and marks each job.
Part four: one question. In your own words, what is this app for? There is no wrong answer. We want to know what you understood.
Before every challenge, you will be someone else. A card says Pretend you are, and tells you who you are and what problem you have today. Try to think like that person.

Now, coins. You earn one coin for every step you answer in the script. You earn ten more coins when you finish and send your report. And when you find a real problem, and Jerry confirms it, you earn five extra coins. Your coins are counted in Kenya shillings. Your group leader will tell you how many shillings each coin is worth.
Here is the most important rule of the whole week. Honesty beats speed.

If you tap It worked too fast, without really trying, the app notices. If you find a real problem and tap It didn't, and explain it, that is worth more than a fast tick. A red cross that finds a real problem earns more than a quick green tick.
If you do not understand something, that is not your fault. Say so. Confusing words and hidden buttons are problems we must fix.

Some practical things. The apps are small, but videos use data, so watch them on Wi-Fi when you can. Use only the made-up names and numbers in the test. Never type your real passwords, your real money details, or private things about yourself or your family.
Our first test, we will do together. It is a small app called Break-Even. It has just one screen with three boxes, so it is a good place to practise the four parts.
Take your time. Be curious. Be honest. Asante sana for helping us build a better bridge.

howATestWorks.name: Explainer video
howATestWorks.what: watch.html?app=<key>&mode=explain — about 4 minutes, recorded voice, the app live beside the captions.

howATestWorks.name: Test script
howATestWorks.what: Testers' List → 🧪 Start the test script (scripts/<key>.json, written separately). One step per card: ✅ It worked / ❌ It didn't / 🤷 Not sure.

howATestWorks.name: Final challenge
howATestWorks.what: kenya/<key>.json challenge: start empty (exact `start`), outcome tasks with no steps, then ✔ Check my work — each task's check reads the app's real saved data. Hints show only after a fail. Must be done in the NORMAL app link, not the 🧪 test copy (the test copy saves to sessionStorage, which the checker cannot see).

howATestWorks.name: In your own words
howATestWorks.what: One free-text answer: 'In your own words, what is this app for?' Jerry reviews against keyIdeas.

coins.existing: From 'Test Script — the standard.md' v1: 1 coin per script step answered · +5 per ❌/🤷 Jerry confirms as a real problem · +10 for finishing and sending the report. KES per coin and the weekly cap are Jerry's choice in Daraja HQ → 🧪 Test scripts → 🎁 Testing reward (currency KES).
coins.proposedForChallenge: PROPOSAL — Jerry to confirm: +2 coins per challenge task passed on the first Check, +1 if passed after a hint, +3 for an own-words answer that hits at least 2 key ideas. Not built anywhere yet.
coins.kesPerCoin: UNSET — Jerry to decide (the video deliberately says 'your group leader will tell you').

honesty: Honesty beats speed: a ❌ that finds a real problem earns more (+5 when confirmed) than a fast ✅ (1). The script runner already flags answers under 6 seconds as ⚡ rushing.

practiceApp.why: The simplest app on the shelf: one screen, three number boxes, answers appear as you type, no tabs, no account, no American-only ideas (a mandazi seller fits perfectly). The challenge has 4 tasks with clear right answers (cost 6, monthly 2,400, lowest price 12), so the group can learn how Check my work and hints behave together.
practiceApp.doTogether: Leader plays kenya/breakeven.json's video on one screen, everyone does the script on their own phone, then the challenge step by step with the group talking it through, then everyone writes their own-words answer alone.
